children: , America's largest bank by assets, recruited former CPPIB trading executive Chris Finora to run Canadian Cash Equities Trading. The stock slipped approximately 0.6% to $356.43 Tuesday as financial shares weakened.

The appointment extends an aggressive Canadian expansion. JPMorgan has brought in 18 executives and managing directors over the past year, lifting its director ranks in the country by 20%. Its Canadian workforce has grown roughly 50% in five years, while revenue has almost doubled as the bank won clients and grabbed market share.

The timing is deliberate: Canada wants to attract $1 trillion of investment over five years, and JPMorgan is positioning itself to capture the trading and advisory activity that could follow. Still, the bank produced $24.9 billion of Banking and Markets revenue in the second quarter alone, so Canada must deliver serious capital flows before these hires move the companywide numbers. The valuation snapshot adds another warning: the shares trade 12.74% above the $316.16 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors already pay a meaningful premium for JPMorgan's execution.

title: JPMorgan Slips While Its Canadian Revenue Nearly Doubles
